title: QUIC RFC 9000 Connection ID Sequence and Active-Set Floor
purpose: Describe the bounded S5P1P1 connection-ID sequence, active-set, and replenishment proof floor.
design_summary: The peer connection-ID state treats the initial peer-issued destination connection ID as sequence 0 and the peer preferred-address connection ID as implicit sequence 1. NEW_CONNECTION_ID processing validates duplicate sequence and connection-ID reuse, applies Retire Prior To before enforcing active_connection_id_limit, and reports retired sequence numbers so the runtime can emit RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID. The local issuance path keeps active route and stateless-reset-token state registered until retirement, replenishes retired or newly used issued IDs with the next sequence number when the peer's active limit allows it, and advertises active_connection_id_limit through transport parameters.
data_and_state_considerations: Connection-ID byte values are copied into route/token state before being exposed through effects. Peer-issued CIDs are tracked by sequence, by historical sequence, and by reverse connection-ID lookup so duplicate frames are idempotent while conflicting reuse is rejected. Locally issued CIDs are retired through paired route and stateless-reset-token effects, and replacement NEW_CONNECTION_ID frames are built only after packet protection can send the frame on the active path.
edge_cases_and_constraints: Maximum-length initial destination connection IDs still retire as sequence 0.
Preferred-address CIDs remain sequence 1 across duplicate preferred-address processing and cannot be reused under another sequence number.
Temporary active-set excess is accepted only when Retire Prior To immediately removes enough older CIDs.
Local replenishment does not wrap beyond the maximum QUIC variable-length integer sequence number.
risks: The local-initiated migration pool policy remains separate and is not fully closed by this floor.
The first client-selected Destination Connection ID and Retry-provided CID sequencing rule remains a separate S5P1P1 tail item.

supplemental_sections.heading: Boundary
supplemental_sections.content: This design closes the bounded S5P1P1 sequence and active-set floor only. It does not claim local-initiated migration pool completeness, Retry integrity validation changes, public API widening, or hosted interop readiness.
